findings.message: 119 AC-2 says connecting follows the app's state. The diff moves three consumers off `myGitAccounts().configured` (the chat suggestion, the Overview nudge and the Git accounts page) onto `githubAppStatus().state === "ready"`. Two more readers of the same flag were left on the old rule. (1) The `connect_github` confirm card (`connectCard`) refuses only when `!configured`, which is `hasSecret` alone, so it still offers a Connect card when the app is incomplete or unreadable. (2) `get_my_git_identities` returns `configured: true` for an incomplete app, and the tool describes that field as "whether GitHub is set up". That leaves two copies of the "can a person connect" rule, and they disagree. Fix: have `connectCard` refuse unless `githubAppStatus(v).state === "ready"`, with the same wording the page uses (NOT_SET_UP for none, APP_NOT_READY otherwise). Either derive `configured` from that state or drop it. Add the card to the `invited()` table in state-119.test.ts.
findings.scenario: An Admin stores an incomplete app value, e.g. `only-the-secret-…`. An Engineer types "Connect my GitHub" in chat. The page, the suggestion and the Overview all hide Connect, but chat still shows a Connect GitHub confirm card. The Engineer confirms and the run fails with APP_INCOMPLETE. `get_my_git_identities` meanwhile tells the agent that GitHub is set up.

findings.message: The new APP_NOT_READY doc comment went in under the existing "116 AC-6" JSDoc. Now two JSDoc blocks sit on top of each other above APP_NOT_READY, and APP_INCOMPLETE has lost its comment. Fix: put the 119 comment and APP_NOT_READY above the 116 AC-6 comment, so that comment sits directly above APP_INCOMPLETE again.

`setAppCheckMs` is a mutable module-global setter exported from production code, and only tests use it. Any importer can change the cache lifetime for every tenant in the process. Make it a test seam instead, e.g. inject the clock or lifetime through the test setup, or move it behind a non-exported test helper.
